definition: A hormone is a body chemical that can affect mental and physical functioning. In this context, melatonin is a hormone that helps regulate the normal sleep–wake cycle, and altered levels are linked with seasonal affective disorder.

reasons: The definition’s general claim that “a hormone is a body chemical that can affect mental and physical functioning” is not supported by the supplied packet text (the packet only describes melatonin as a hormone).

The packet supports that “altered levels of melatonin” relate to SAD and specifically that winter-pattern SAD involves producing too much melatonin, but the definition states this as a general linkage (“altered levels are linked with seasonal affective disorder”) without enough explicit support for the full phrasing.

The packet supports melatonin as a hormone important for maintaining the normal sleep–wake cycle and notes altered levels in relation to seasonal affective disorder, but it does not support the broad general definition of a hormone as a body chemical that affects mental and physical functioning.
